title: Check if Strings Can be Made Equal With Operations I
summary: Given two strings s1 and s2, both of length 4 and consisting of lowercase English letters, you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Choose any two indices i and j such that j - i = 2, and swap the characters at these indices in either string.
statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, both of length 4 and consisting of lowercase English letters, you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Choose any two indices i and j such that j - i = 2, and swap the characters at these indices in either string. Determine whether it is possible to make the strings s1 and s2 equal through these operations. Return true if they can be made equal, and false otherwise.
constraints: Both strings contain exactly four lowercase characters.
An operation may swap positions zero and two or positions one and three any number of times.
Return whether s1 can be transformed into s2.
reference_solution:
def can_swap_same_parity_indices(s1,s2):
    return sorted(s1[::2])==sorted(s2[::2]) and sorted(s1[1::2])==sorted(s2[1::2])
hints: Allowed swaps never move a character between even and odd indices.
Within each two-position parity group, arbitrary order is reachable.
Sort and compare the two even-position multisets and the two odd-position multisets.
Matching both invariant groups is necessary, and the permitted swap realizes either ordering inside each group, so it is sufficient.
